stem: An adolescent boy is being assessed for delayed puberty and is short for age with normal growth velocity, no pubertal growth spurt yet, and a delayed bone age, which diagnosis best fits this pattern?

options.text: Constitutional delay of growth and puberty

explanation: Constitutional delay of growth and puberty is the best fit. Normal growth velocity with delayed skeletal maturation and delayed pubertal development is typical of this normal variant.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because familial short stature usually has a normal bone age and normal timing of puberty, with height tracking along a lower percentile.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because constitutional delay of growth and puberty typically presents with short stature, normal growth velocity, delayed bone age, and late pubertal onset with a later pubertal growth spurt.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because skeletal dysplasia usually causes disproportionate short stature and abnormal body proportions rather than isolated delayed puberty with normal growth velocity.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because Crohn disease is a systemic illness that can cause poor weight gain and reduced growth velocity rather than an isolated constitutional pattern.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because primary hypothyroidism can delay growth and puberty, but it usually causes a reduced growth rate and other features of hypothyroidism rather than normal growth velocity.
